# Nell Harcourt

## Overview

- **Age:** 20  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011), [v3 c19 P0](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0000)</sub>

- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v3 c41 P15](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0015)</sub>

## Appearance

Nell possesses a slender, straight-backed frame with a small, white face, a small pointed chin, a pleasant nose, and star-like gray eyes. Her glowing hair, which was bright red and cropped during her youth, matures into a rich auburn plait. She often wears dresses in shades of green and white that complement her fair complexion.

## Personality

Nell is an imaginative, passionate, and energetic individual prone to high romantic expectations and deep reveries. She is generous and unselfish, though she possesses a swift temper and an intensity of affection and dislike that can cause her to harbor animosity. She works diligently and resolutely to overcome challenges and achieve academic success.

## History

Nell spent her early childhood being raised by Mrs. Thomas and later Mrs. Rudge, enduring hard work and loneliness until being placed in the Marden orphan asylum. She was taken in from the asylum by Thirza Abernethy to reside at Grey Shutters in Brierley. At the local school, she established a close friendship with Isolde Pembroke and entered into an intense academic competition with Hugh Carrow. Nell went on to study at Regent's Academy, taking Second Year work to earn her First Class teacher's license within a single year and winning the Avery scholarship. She subsequently served as schoolteacher in Brierley and co-founded the Brierley Village Improvement Society, acting as its secretary. Later, Nell enrolled at Wexcombe College alongside her friend Honora Hollis, living with prospective housemates at Tabby's Place while pursuing her Senior year studies in English and publishing creative stories.

_Sources: [v1 c5 P13](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0013), [v1 c5 P14](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0014), [v1 c5 P15](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0015), [v1 c12 P40](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0040), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v1 c36 P41](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0041), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c11 P0](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0000), [v3 c4 P2](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0002), [v3 c9 P0](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0000), [v3 c15 P0](../source/v03-c15.md#nw-v03-c15-p0000), [v3 c16 P2](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0002), [v3 c35 P28](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- born in Harborough, Nova Scotia to high school teachers Edmund and Bertha Harcourt  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011)</sub>
- orphaned in infancy after both parents died of fever  <sub>[v1 c5 P13](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0013)</sub>
- raised by Mrs. Thomas until age eight assisting with children  <sub>[v1 c5 P13](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0013), [v1 c5 P14](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0014)</sub>
- lived upriver with Mrs. Rudge for over two years  <sub>[v1 c5 P14](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0014), [v1 c5 P15](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0015)</sub>
- spent four months in the Marden orphan asylum before being taken in by Thirza Abernethy  <sub>[v1 c5 P15](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0015), [v1 c29 P32](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0032)</sub>
- attempted to dye her hair green during her early years at Grey Shutters  <sub>[v1 c27 P16](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0016), [v1 c37 P31](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0031)</sub>

## Quotes

> I turned eleven this past March,” Nell stated, giving in to plain reality with a faint sigh. “And Nova Scotia’s Harborough is where I was born.  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011)</sub>

> I really hoped for a white dress featuring puffed sleeves,” she murmured gloomily. “I asked God for one, though I didn't actually anticipate it because of that.  <sub>[v1 c11 P14](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0014)</sub>

> Oh, Mrs. Sowerby, my regret is so immense,” she uttered while her voice trembled slightly. “Even exhaustively reciting every word in a dictionary would fail to convey the full extent of my remorse.  <sub>[v1 c10 P30](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0030)</sub>

> Well, a person is unable to abandon the routine of being a small girl immediately,” Nell said cheerfully.  <sub>[v2 c10 P4](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0004)</sub>

> It is amazing to realize that I am turning twenty today and have permanently bidden farewell to my teenage years  <sub>[v3 c19 P0](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0000)</sub>
